concerns.text: T023 specifies 'Iterate thresholds from a minimum to a maximum value in uniform steps' but fails to name the concrete deliverable (the specific range 0.0–1.0 and step 0.1) mandated by FR-006. An implementer cannot execute this deterministically without guessing the sweep parameters.

T024 specifies 'Execute a sufficient number of episodes' which is not a concrete deliverable. FR-003 explicitly mandates 'exactly 1,000 simulated episodes'. The task must be rewritten to enforce this specific count to ensure statistical power.

T028 mentions 'Linear/Quadratic' regression but omits the explicit requirement to implement ANOVA and statistical significance testing (p < 0.05) required by SC-001 and SC-004. The task description does not provide the implementer with the necessary logic to verify the success criteria.

T030 relies on 'mean log-probability shift (from T021)', but T021 only promises 'logging' of shifts. There is no task explicitly defining the aggregation logic to calculate the mean shift required for the 'distillation cost-benefit ratio' formula. The implementer lacks the source data definition.

T015 mandates 'mandatory caching logic' for generated graphs. This contradicts Constitution Principle I (Reproducibility) and Principle III (Data Hygiene) which require graphs to be 'regenerated on-the-fly' or fetched from a canonical source to ensure fresh execution. The task as written risks violating the reproducibility constraint.

T029 describes implementing 'inflection point detection logic' as a separate algorithmic step. However, FR-006 and SC-001 define the inflection point as a result of the statistical regression (quadratic term significance). The task description is ambiguous and risks implementing a heuristic detector instead of the required statistical derivation.
